Hallie Shoffner

Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, Arkansas · Challenger

Farmer; former manager of her family's rice and soybean farm

Hallie Shoffner is a farmer from northeast Arkansas who managed her family's rice and soybean farm and a seed company, and founded an agricultural food hub. She launched her campaign for U.S. Senate in July 2025. She won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Lewisville Mayor Ethan Dunbar with about 78% of the vote and faces Republican incumbent Tom Cotton and Libertarian Jeff Wadlin on November 3, 2026.

Where Shoffner stands

Agriculture and farm policy
Supports farm policy that encourages growing a wider range of crops and public-private partnerships to build processing facilities near farm communities. Calls for passing a Farm Bill.
Farmland consolidation
Says too much farmland consolidation by corporations, private equity and wealthy people should be treated as an antitrust violation. Proposes farmland trusts, low-interest loans for young farmers and taxes on large consolidators.
Health care and Medicaid
Supports expanding Medicare coverage, raising Medicaid reimbursement rates, and investing in telehealth, federally qualified health centers and more medical residencies. Says Medicaid is economic infrastructure for rural hospitals.
Immigration
Says she has a "serious problem" with ICE's level of funding and supports putting resources toward the immigration court backlog. Says undocumented immigrants should be deported if they commit a crime with a victim, not solely for being undocumented.
Iran war
Would support ending the war in Iran and has criticized what the war costs Americans.
AI and data centers
Supports federal AI regulation so products are vetted for consumer safety before reaching the market. Says data centers should sign community development agreements with local governments.
Economy, labor and education
Campaign platform pledges to lower the cost of living, keep jobs in Arkansas, support workers and strengthen unions, and pay teachers and school staff more.

Background

  • Born August 31, 1987; grew up south of Newport, Arkansas; lives in Little Rock
  • Master's degree in public service, Clinton School of Public Service (Little Rock)
  • Managed her family's rice and soybean farm (closed in 2025) and a seed company; founded an agricultural food hub
  • No prior elected office
  • Won the 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate (Arkansas) on March 3, 2026, with about 78% of the vote
